messages:
sam: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change we saw a 95th->99th latency delta grow ~2.8x during peak QPS. Not constant, seems correlated with longer sequences + kv-cache misses.

maria: Ugh. Any flamegraphs or CPU stacks? Could be the new matmul kernel regressing small-batch throughput.

aj: Pasted a short profiling snapshot from the canary node:
```
# top hotspots (p50/p95/p99):
1) kernel_dispatch: 12ms / 45ms / 120ms
2) kv_cache_lookup: 1ms / 5ms / 20ms
3) batch_formation_lock: 0.8ms / 4.5ms / 18ms
4) context_switch / polling: small but increasing
```
Looks like when kv hit-rate drops, we end up with bigger per-request work in kernel_dispatch and batch lock contention rises.

perfbot: perf-alert: increased tail latency detected on canary pool (kernel v2.3.1) — baseline vs canary: p99 +170%.

chris: My theory: continuous-batching heuristic currently uses fixed `max_wait_ms=8` and naive token-budget of `500`. When long sequences combine with a few cache-miss items, the actual token work balloons and stalls others. Two knobs to try: make admission token-aware and add a soft-token-cap per-queue window.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: token-budget target => 800 tokens per batch, but enforce a soft admission policy: if adding req would push expected batch token sum > 1100, short-circuit with soft 429 (retry-after few ms) OR route to a high-latency fallback shard.

aj: Rough admission pseudo-config:
```
admission:
  mode: token_budget
  target_tokens: 800
  soft_limit: 1100
  soft_action: soft_429  # return 429 with X-Retry-After-ms=10
  hard_limit: 2000
  hard_action: reject
  max_wait_ms: 6    # shorten to favor quicker batches
```
Behavior: accept while current_batch_tokens + estimated_req_tokens <= target; if between target and soft_limit -> accept with probability p (to randomize), else soft_429.

chris: Also add per-client short lease token accounting so a big multi-turn chat doesn't hog admission for many small requests. TTL the per-client token lease at 500ms to give fairness.

maria: For KV cache: add a fast-path for small kv lookups during admission to estimate additional token overhead (cache miss penalty ~+30 tokens). If lookup fails, treat req as heavier. Also bump kv-cache admission prefetch to reduce miss bursts.

aj: Metrics we need for the experiment: p50/p95/p99 latency, batch token distribution, batch size distribution, kv-hit-rate, admission_decision_counts (accepted/soft_429/hard_reject/reroute), queue_length_by_shard, per-client_token_leases_active.

sam: Can we run canary in dedicated pool only (not all hosted) and run 1% traffic for 4h then 30m steady-state? If numbers good, promote. Also need rollback plan to revert kernel or admission policy.

maria: I'll own the canary. Plan: 1) deploy admission patch + max_wait tweak + kv prefetch on dedicated canary pool; 2) run synthetic microbench replay (short/long sequences mixed) for 30m; 3) open for 1% prod traffic for 4h; 4) gather metrics and follow checklist.

chris: Quick experiment variant: try probabilistic admission rather than immediate soft_429 for medium-over-budget cases — e.g., accept with p = 0.6 between target and soft_limit. That might reduce client retries. We'll compare both.

aj: Note: instrument code to tag each request with `admit_reason` so logs/debugger can correlate tail events. Add trace span around `admission_decide -> batch_enqueue -> kernel_dispatch` to catch where the tail originates.

perfbot: experiment-created: admission-token-canary-2026-02-18 by maria; expected windows: 4h live after synthetic.

sam: Thanks. If we still see p99 regressions after admission, next step is rollback kernel-select heuristics and run per-kernel microbench. For now focus on token-aware admission and kv prefetching.

maria: I'll post results thread when we have the first 30m synthetic run. :white_check_mark:
